_how_this_works: The code standards this service is held to, as numbers. `baseline` is FROZEN: it records every limit and every ledger exactly as code health H4 found them on 2026-09-19, and it is never maintained. `budget` is the live limit; it starts identical to `baseline` and may only ever get TIGHTER. `src/lib/__tests__/codeStandards.test.ts` asserts all of it on every run, and since H2 that suite runs inside the Cloud Build deploy gate, so a change that breaks a standard cannot ship. If a test here told you to lower a number or remove a line, edit `budget` and only `budget` — never raise a limit, and never add a name to a ledger. THE ONE EXCEPTION IS A MOVE: see `_moved`.
_moved_how_this_works: Every ledger here is keyed on a FILE PATH, so a file that MOVES orphans its entry — the same debt at the new path is unlisted (which fails) and cannot be added (a ledger may only shrink). `_moved` is how a key follows its code: each record names ONE key the frozen `baseline` already holds (`from`) and ONE key it does not (`to`), and the tests read the baseline THROUGH it. A relabel is all it can do — the ledger's length is the same number either side, and `budget <= baseline` then holds the new key to exactly the room the old one had. So a move buys NOTHING: not a bigger number, not an extra member, not a merge onto a key that already exists, and not a path that is not a real file. ⚠ `_moved` is a SIBLING of `baseline`, never a part of it, so declaring an honest move does NOT move `BASELINE_SHA256` — H11's hand re-pin was the loophole, not the fix. Prune a record once the budget line it follows is gone. TD-272.

budget._first_load_js_note: KILOBYTES OF JAVASCRIPT A VISITOR DOWNLOADS BEFORE A ROUTE CAN DO ANYTHING (code health H18, closing TD-281). Recorded from a real `next build` on 2026-09-20, after H17 cut the median route from 478.5 kB to 255.5 kB and after H18 closed TD-280. ⚠ 87.2 kB IS THE FLOOR under every route — React, the Next runtime and the shared chunk — so no target below that is reachable by any change. The ledger lists only the routes AT OR ABOVE the 300 kB ceiling in `scripts/bundle-budget.js`; everything else is held by `first_load_js_median_kb`, which is what broad creep moves. ⚠ NOTHING IN JEST MEASURES THESE. The reader is `scripts/bundle-budget.js` and it runs in the Cloud Build deploy gate (`cloudbuild.yaml`, the `test` step) and locally as `npm run bundle-budget`; `codeStandards.test.ts` asserts the wiring, because a budget nobody runs reads as enforced and is not. ── TD-300 (2026-09-28): WHAT THE HEADROOM IS AND WHAT EATS IT. The median was 256 with 44 of 87 routes at or under it — the median WAS the 44th route, so the next byte on any route at 256 would have turned the deploy gate red for a reason unrelated to that change. The fix took weight off instead of raising the number: the three Supabase clients are now AUTH-ONLY (src/lib/supabaseAuthClient.ts), because supabase-js's createClient builds Realtime, PostgREST, Storage and Functions in its constructor and so could never tree-shake — 29 kB off 73 routes. The median is 227 kB and is recorded at 229, the 2 kB the ratchet itself tolerates (MEDIAN_SLACK_KB); at 229, 50 routes are at or under it, so SIX routes may each cross it before the median does. `npm run bundle-budget` now prints that count on every run (the tightness note) — watch it, not the median. ⚠ The median is still a CROWD: payments, payments/[id] and sources sit at 227, seven routes within 1 kB. What eats headroom is anything every page imports — the shared admin chunk, the root providers, the i18n catalogue (en.json, 96 kB gz, still on 74 routes). ⚠ AND WHAT THIS FIGURE DOES NOT COUNT: Next's printed first-load for an app route is the PAGE entry only; chunks that only a LAYOUT loads (the root layout's React Query provider, 8.8 kB gz; the admin layout's menu and scope code) are downloaded on first paint and are not in it. /login prints 87.6 kB and the browser fetches ~230. Moving weight from a page into a layout lowers this number without making anything lighter — see TD-304. ── TD-352 (2026-10-06): the 2,480-school list behind SchoolSelect (~30 kB gz, chunk shared by /scholarship/apply, /profile and /onboarding/profile only) now loads by import() on the field's first pointer-over, touch or focus; the two budgeted lines were LOWERED to the measured figure plus about 1 kB: /profile 300 → 271 (269.755), /scholarship/apply 272 → 244 (242.551).
